The primary evidence establishing the efficacy of larotrectinib in patients with solid tumors harboring an *NTRK* gene fusion comes from three single-arm trials: LOXO-TRK-14001, LOXO-TRK 15002, LOXO-TRK 15003 (also referred to as “14001”, “15002”, and “15003”, respectively).

citations.quote: LOXO-TRK-14001, entitled “A Phase 1 Study of the Oral TRK Inhibitor LOXO-101 in Adult Patients with Solid Tumors”,

result.text: ORR 75% (95% CI: 61%, 85%), including 22% complete response and 53% partial response; among 41 responders, 73% had DOR of at least 6 months and 39% had DOR over a year; median DOR not reached

citations.quote: the overall response rate (ORR) was 75% (95% CI: 61%, 85%), including 22% of patients with a complete response (CR) and 53% of patients with a partial response (PR) to larotrectinib.
Among the 41 responding patients, 73% had a duration of response (DOR) of at least 6 months and 39% had a DOR of over a year.
At the time of the analysis, the median DOR had not been reached, and response duration ranged from 1.6 to 33.2 months.

indication.text: VITRAKVI is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors that have an NTRK gene fusion without a known acquired resistance mutation, are metastatic or where surgical resection is likely to result in severe morbidity, and have no satisfactory alternative treatments or that have progressed following treatment

citations.quote: VITRAKVI is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors that:

are metastatic or where surgical resection is likely to result in severe morbidity, and
have no satisfactory alternative treatments or that have progressed following treatment.

target_moa.text: Kinase inhibitor that inhibits the kinase activities of the tropomyosin receptor kinases TRKA, TRKB, and TRKC; strong scientific rationale that inhibition of TRK causes shrinkage of tumors with NTRK fusions

citations.quote: Larotrectinib (previously called LOXO-101) is a kinase inhibitor that inhibits the kinase activities of the tropomyosin receptor kinases TRKA, TRKB, and TRKC.
For larotrectinib, there was a strong scientific rationale that the inhibition of TRK would cause shrinkage of tumors with *NTRK* fusions.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) in order of decreasing frequency were fatigue, nausea, dizziness, vomiting, anemia, increased AST, cough, increased ALT, constipation, and diarrhea. Primary serious risks are hepatotoxicity and neurotoxicity: increased transaminases of any grade in 45% (Grade 3 AST/ALT in 6%); neurologic adverse reactions of any grade in 53% (Grade 3 and 4 in 6% and 0.6%)

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (\ge 20\%) in order of decreasing frequency were fatigue, nausea, dizziness, vomiting, anemia, increased AST, cough, increased ALT, constipation, and diarrhea.
increased transaminases of any grade occurred in 45%, including Grade 3 increased AST or ALT in 6% of patients.
Neurologic adverse reactions of any grade occurred in 53% of patients, including Grade 3 and Grade 4 neurologic adverse reactions in 6% and 0.6% of patients, respectively.

detail.text: No FDA-approved test for the detection of NTRK gene fusion is currently available; patients selected based on presence of NTRK gene fusion in tumor specimens (most enrolled by local NGS testing). A PMC was planned to develop a companion diagnostic.

citations.quote: Select patients for treatment with VITRAKVI based on the presence of a *NTRK* gene fusion in tumor specimens [see *Clinical Studies (14)*]. An FDA-approved test for the detection of *NTRK* gene fusion is not currently available.
A PMC is planned to develop a companion diagnostic (see section 4.4).

description.text: Updated prescribing information with response data from patients with NTRK fusion solid tumors and expanded safety population; labeling changes and fulfillment of postmarketing requirement (no new indication).

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for revisions to the prescribing information (PI) updating the response data from patients with NTRK fusion solid tumors. Additionally, labeling changes were made to Adverse Reactions (Section 6.1) and Pediatric Use (Section 8.4) based on updated safety data expanding the safety population. Warnings and Precautions Section 5.1 was updated to "Central Nervous System Effects" with language to clarify cognitive impairment and other disorders and to Section 5.2 to update "Skeletal Fractures" language. Finally, edits to associated with the previously described edits were made to the Patient Information and Instructions for Use.
